description: Curated mapping of common VB6-era COM ProgIDs to modern .NET 10 replacements. Shipped as in-prompt context for the vb6 extraction prompts (vb6/dotnet10-winforms, -blazor, -minapi). The replacement_hint for each entry varies by target paradigm — the prompts pick the matching line at extraction time.

entries.winforms: Microsoft.Office.Interop.Excel (legacy interop) for active Excel UI scenarios; ClosedXML 0.105+ for headless workbook authoring.
entries.blazor: ClosedXML 0.105+ exclusively. Excel Interop requires user-interactive STA threads; not viable in Blazor Server.
entries.minapi: ClosedXML 0.105+. Excel Interop is not viable in a headless service.
entries.notes: ClosedXML produces .xlsx (Open XML); legacy .xls output is possible but rare. Confirm target file format during Discovery.

entries.winforms: DocX (xceedsoftware/DocX) for headless docx authoring; Microsoft.Office.Interop.Word for active Word UI.
entries.blazor: DocX or Open XML SDK exclusively.
entries.minapi: DocX or Open XML SDK exclusively.
entries.notes: DocX has the smaller API surface; Open XML SDK is the closer-to-the-metal option.

entries.winforms: Microsoft.Graph (REST) for cloud-mailbox scenarios; MailKit for SMTP/IMAP if on-prem.
entries.blazor: Microsoft.Graph (REST). MailKit for SMTP/IMAP if on-prem.
entries.minapi: Microsoft.Graph (REST) or MailKit. Outlook Interop is not viable headless.
entries.notes: Microsoft.Graph is the modern path for hosted Exchange / Microsoft 365. MailKit covers raw SMTP/IMAP.

entries.winforms: EF Core 10 with the appropriate provider (Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer, .Sqlite, .Jet, etc.).
entries.blazor: EF Core 10 with DbContext per scope. Scoped DbContext registration via AddDbContextFactory.
entries.minapi: EF Core 10 for typed access; Dapper for high-throughput batch routines.
entries.notes: EF Core 10 includes a Jet/.mdb provider via Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Jet for legacy MDB compatibility.

entries.winforms: EF Core 10 with Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Jet provider for .mdb compatibility.
entries.notes: DAO 3.6 is the most common; DAO 12.0 ships with Access 2007+. Both target .mdb / .accdb.

entries.winforms: FileSystemObject → System.IO (File, Directory, Path); Dictionary → System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary<string, object>.
entries.notes: Direct 1:1 mapping; no licensing or behavioural risk.

entries.winforms: Process.Start for command execution; SHGetSpecialFolderPath equivalents in System.Environment.GetFolderPath.
entries.blazor: Process.Start in an IHostedService context; flag any UI-spawning calls as Open Question (no user session on the server).
entries.minapi: Process.Start in an IHostedService. SendKeys-style automation is out of scope.
entries.notes: WScript.Shell's RegRead / RegWrite map to Microsoft.Win32.Registry (Windows only).
Strong move toward async/await; legacy synchronous calls become await client.GetAsync(...).

entries.winforms: System.Xml.Linq (XDocument) for LINQ-friendly access; System.Xml.XmlDocument for closer-to-DOM porting.
entries.notes: XDocument is the modern choice. XmlDocument is closer to the legacy DOM shape.

entries.winforms: System.IO.MemoryStream for in-memory; System.IO.FileStream for file.
entries.notes: ADODB.Stream's text-vs-binary mode maps to encoding choice on StreamReader/StreamWriter.
CDO is the legacy Collaboration Data Objects API; MailKit is the modern SMTP client. System.Net.Mail.SmtpClient is now obsolete.

entries.winforms: Playwright for .NET (PlaywrightSharp) for headless browser scenarios; WebView2 for embedded.
entries.blazor: Playwright for .NET headless. WebView2 is not viable server-side.
entries.notes: Internet Explorer is end-of-life. Any IE-COM use is a flag for an architectural rethink — Open Question with the SME.

fallback_guidance: When a ProgID does not appear in this registry, the LLM must emit an open_questions entry naming the ProgID and asking the SME to provide a modern equivalent during Discovery. Do NOT guess — fabricated replacement_hints have caused real production drift on prior engagements.
